subject: Question: change control + ephemeral keychain evidence for SDLC
messages:
From: Claire Huang <claire.huang@finara-bank.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Finara Security Assessor <assessors@finara.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence request: ephemeral keychain & change-control details

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for taking the time on the compliance call yesterday. As part of our SIG/SOC2 intake we need a short packet showing how Redwood handles: code review sampling, CI/CD controls around deploy-time secrets, and your "ephemeral keychain" pattern (rotation, custody, and change approval).

Specifically can you provide:
- a short explanation of the ephemeral keystore workflow (who can request keys, TTLs, and rotation cadence)
- recent audit logs showing a rotation event (redacted where necessary)
- an example code-review sampling export for Q2 2028
- your CI/CD runbook describing how ephemeral secrets are injected and revoked during deploys

We need this for our assessor review by EOD Thursday 2028-07-26. If some items are sensitive, a redacted version is fine as long as the audit trail timestamps and actor names are preserved (we can accept role-based identifiers).

Thanks,
Claire Huang
Senior Security Analyst
Finara Bank

--
Finara Security Assessor Team
assessors@finara.com

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.inference.com>
To: Claire Huang <claire.huang@finara-bank.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence request: ephemeral keychain & change-control details

Hi Claire,

Acknowledged — we'll assemble a scoped package. Irene, can you pull the rotation audit PDF and the Q2 code-review sample? Marissa, can you attach the CI/CD runbook that covers ephemeral secret injection?

Quick clarifications from our side:
- When you say "actor names" are preserved, do you need full emails or role mappings (e.g., infra-ops@redwood vs John Doe)? We can provide role mappings if helpful.
- For rotation events, do you want a sample that shows a full rotation (key old->new) or the rotation audit that shows TTL expiry + re-issue?

We aim to ship a redacted bundle within 6 hours but will prioritize the rotation audit and the runbook first.

Thanks — LW

Logan Wright
Manager, Compliance Intake
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.inference.com>, Claire Huang <claire.huang@finara-bank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence request: ephemeral keychain & change-control details

Hi all,

Attaching the requested items — redacted where required. Summary below and notes on redaction: see attached files for timestamps and actor IDs.

Attachments included:
- code-review-sampling-2028-Q2.csv (sample exports from our PR sampling job; contains PR IDs, reviewer role, and outcome)
- keystore-rotation-audit-202807.pdf (audit log from the keystore service; usernames replaced with role tags such as infra-operator and release-bot; operation IDs preserved)
- ci-cd-runbook-ephemeral-keys.md (runbook excerpt describing inject/revoke steps, vault policies, and environment variable hygiene)

Redaction notes:
- We replaced personal emails with role identifiers per your allowance (e.g., infra-ops@redwood).
- IP addresses and pod names were redacted; operation IDs and timestamps retained.
- For the full rotation trace we included a timestamped event chain (rotate-request -> key-issue -> revoke-old) but scrubbed any internal resource ARNs.

Answers to Logan's questions:
- Role mappings should be sufficient for your assessment — we can provide full email addresses under NDA if required.
- The PDF shows a rotation event chain (full rotate-request -> new key provision -> old revoke). That should demonstrate both scheduled and on-demand rotations.

Claire — please confirm if this granularity works for Thursday's assessor review. If you need additional artifacts (SRE runbook sign-off or PagerDuty incident snapshots), call that out and we'll add them.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Senior Security Engineer, Platform
Redwood Inference

[Attachment stubs]
- code-review-sampling-2028-Q2.csv (CSV, 43KB)
- keystore-rotation-audit-202807.pdf (PDF, 120KB)
- ci-cd-runbook-ephemeral-keys.md (Markdown, 18KB)

From: Claire Huang <claire.huang@finara-bank.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence request: ephemeral keychain & change-control details

Irene — thank you, this looks good and should be sufficient for the initial assessor pass. The role mappings and retained operation IDs meet our requirements. A couple of small asks before we close the ticket: 

- Can you add a one-paragraph note in the runbook that states your TTL defaults and the escalation path for failed rotations (who is paged first)? That helps the assessor understand the human controls.
- For the code-review sampling CSV, can you include one line that indicates the sampling policy (e.g., 10% of PRs flagged for manual sampling) — either as a header row or a separate small text file.

If you can drop those two small additions by end of day that would be ideal. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Claire Huang
Senior Security Analyst
Finara Bank
